documents.title: Using Generative AI Reflectively and Responsibly in Teaching and Learning
tiers: Limited use of AI in class with citation
documents.summary: A teaching-center guide explaining what generative AI is, why it matters (student use, benefits, bias, environmental cost) and how instructors can build and communicate a course policy. It offers three sample syllabus statements and advice on equity and accessibility, but sets no rule for students.
documents.stance_why: The guide does not ban or permit AI itself; it says "Make your course's GenAI policy clear in your syllabus" and offers three sample statements (not permitting, limited with citation, permitting AI "with no restrictions") for instructors to adapt. The decision is left to instructors, with tiers listed.

units.why: This sentence defines AI ("development of computer systems that can perform tasks typically requiring human intellectual activities"), setting what the guide covers; P61 definitions.

units.why: This sentence defines generative AI as "focused on creating new data" (text, images, code), which sets the scope of the guidance; P61.

notes: Coder B. Both documents are TLC guidance; the sample syllabus statements are templates adapted from UIC, so their rules are coded as unit_stance of the template, with the document stance delegates. The same three statements appear in both documents and are coded in each, as each document is coded on its own. Cross-document links (Academic Integrity, suspected-misconduct guidance, Academic Senate) were not part of the saved text.
